resources.string: Pass level %1$s of %2$s at %3$s to open this map.
This map is still being written. It arrives in a later release.
About a minute, two measurements: how loud your strokes are, and how late the click reaches your headphones. It stays on the map if you skip it.
Half a minute so the app can hear your strokes on the pad. Connect headphones and run it again to get the click as well. It stays on the map if you skip it.
Sound check. Teaches the app your pad and your headphones. Can be replayed at any time.

Click on the speaker — scores are wrong
The microphone hears the click and counts it as your stroke, so the result means nothing. Use headphones for the click.

The click leaves through the speaker, and the microphone that listens for your strokes hears it. Nothing can be filtered out: the click lands exactly on the note it marks, and on a practice pad it is louder than your stroke, so the app cannot tell them apart. It scores the click as a stroke, hides the real one behind it, and the accuracy, stars and timing you get afterwards describe the click instead of your playing — one recorded run had 37 of 88 detected strokes coming from the app itself.
Better never to turn this on. The one case where it holds: you know your microphone cannot hear the speaker — an external microphone far from the phone, or the sound routed to a speaker out of its reach. Otherwise wear headphones for the click, or leave the click off and play by the moving notes.
Adds the millisecond offset under each verdict.
Practice needs the microphone to hear your strokes.
Could not start audio. Close other apps using the microphone and try again.
Audio stopped mid-run: the output changed or another app took the microphone. Press play to start again.
The microphone part moves your strokes back to where you played them; the rest moves the notes and the click together, so what you see and what you hear reach the line at the same moment.
Not measured yet \u2014 run the sound check.
%1$s and its measured latency will be removed. The next sound check on these headphones starts from scratch.

%1$d outputs are all there is room for. Delete one to save another.
Steady enough \u2014 press Stop to keep it, or keep playing.
The strokes scatter a lot. Play more evenly, or reset and try again.
Could not start audio. Close other apps using the microphone and try again.

Enough strokes \u2014 the value is stored. Reset to measure again.
Not measured yet in this visit.
Room %1$d dB, your strokes %2$d dB. The gate sits between them.
Microphone level with the gate mark
%1$d strokes landed too far from a click to be a round trip.
Most of your strokes did not land near a note. That is the sound, not your playing \u2014 run the sound check.
%1$d%% of your strokes were too quiet to count. Play a little harder, or move the phone closer to the pad.
More strokes than notes: %1$d%% extra. A rebounding stick or a noisy room \u2014 both are heard as strokes.
You play %1$d ms behind the click, every stroke. Aim to hit with the click, not after it.
You play %1$d ms ahead of the click, every stroke. Let the click arrive before the stick.
Your evenness alone is worth %1$d%%: that is what this level scores once the lateness is gone.
You speed up: by the end you are %1$d ms ahead of where you started.
You slow down: by the end you are %1$d ms behind where you started.
Your strokes wander by \u00b1%1$d ms. Drop the tempo until they stop wandering, then bring it back.
Even, and nothing to fix at this tempo. Take the next one.
%1$.0f\u00d7 its own measurement error \u2014 too consistent to be chance.
Only %1$.0f\u00d7 its own error: not proven, so nothing is said about it.
Fewer than %1$d counted strokes: too few for any of this to mean anything.

Any headphones will do — the click plays only into them, because a speaker would put it into the microphone and it would be scored as your stroke. With a click the levels also train your timing; without one the notes still roll and you play what you see.

Nothing else to check: the click can only play into headphones. Through the speaker the microphone would hear it and count it as a stroke, so it stays silent.\n\nLevels work anyway \u2014 the notes roll to the line and you play what you see.
Connect the headphones you practise with and open this check again. It sets them up in about fifteen seconds, and the click plays in them from then on.
Nothing to hold against the microphone? Drag it here, then play a level: if the app reads your strokes early, the number is too high.
Put the phone next to the pad. Keep quiet for a moment, then play 8 strokes as you normally would.

Nothing plays in this step. The app listens to the room first, then to your strokes, and puts a gate between the two.\n\nThe mark on the bar is that gate: anything quieter is ignored, here and in a level. The headphones step counts only what is above it, so this one comes first.
Keep quiet for a moment: listening to the room.
Now play 8 strokes at your normal loudness (%1$d of %2$d).
The room is almost as loud as your strokes. It will work, but somewhere quieter works better.
Take one earcup off, hold it against the phone\u2019s microphone and keep still. You play nothing here.

The bar above is live: it moves with every sound the phone hears. Hold the earcup against the bottom edge of the phone, next to the charging port, and press Start — the click begins then, and the bar has to jump with it. If it stays flat, move the earcup and press Start again.
No free hand? Play one stroke on every click instead \u2014 less precise, and it takes about half a minute.

The app plays a click and hears its own click come back, so it measures the headphones without you playing at all. Held against the microphone it repeats to a fraction of a millisecond and stops on its own after about fifteen seconds.

Playing along by hand works too, but your own timing goes into the number: it comes out lower than the headphones really are, and it needs about half a minute of even strokes.

The number is kept per output, so this does not need repeating unless you switch to another pair.
Keep still \u2014 listening. It stops on its own.
The headphones changed, so this round was measuring an output that is gone. Press Start to measure the one connected now.
Nothing was heard. Hold the earcup closer to the microphone, turn the headphone volume up, or lower the gate in the loudness step.
%1$d onsets were too quiet to count. Hold the earcup closer, or lower the gate.

%1$s is connected for the first time. Every pair delays the click by its own amount, and levels are scored against that delay, so the app has to measure this one before it can judge your strokes on it. About half a minute: hold an earcup to the microphone and play eight strokes. Loudness on the pad stays as it was measured.
Microphone level with the gate mark
Could not start audio. Close other apps using the microphone and try again.
The app listens to your pad to know when you hit it. Audio is never recorded or sent anywhere.
Heard you clearly. The phone can tell your strokes from the room.
Hold the earcup against the microphone, then press Start.
Headphones checked \u2014 saved for \u201c%1$s\u201d. This does not need repeating unless you switch to another pair.

A stroke takes %1$d ms to come back through the microphone; the click takes %2$d ms to reach your ears. The app now moves your strokes by the first and the notes by the second, so both land on the line together.
Press Start and hit the pad once on every click, eight times. This one tells you whether the two measurements hold up.

The two steps before this one measured the room and the headphones with the microphone. This step measures the whole thing the way a level does: the click plays, you strike, and the phone reports where your strokes landed.

If they land on the click, the setup is right and nothing else needs doing. If all eight land the same distance off it, that distance is what the headphone measurement got wrong — measure it again. Spread that is not the same distance every time is playing, not setup, and this step does not judge it.
Press Start when you are ready.
That is all of it. The levels are open.
Nothing looks off \u2014 your strokes sat on the click.
Your strokes sat behind the click. The setup looks fine \u2014 playing behind the click is what everybody does at first, and it is exactly what the levels train.
Your strokes sat ahead of the click. The setup looks fine \u2014 running ahead of the click is ordinary at first, and it is exactly what the levels train.

Your strokes came back further from the click than any player can be off. That is the audio path, not your hands \u2014 measure the headphones again, and if it repeats, the numbers are in the check log.
Only %1$d strokes were heard out of eight. That is the pad step, not the headphones \u2014 go back and set the loudness again.
You can walk this check again whenever you like \u2014 nothing here is spent.
A practice-pad drum trainer. Rudiments, a metronome and a microphone that listens to your pad \u2014 nothing else.
Found a bug, or thought of something the app should do? Write to me. Every message goes to one mailbox and is read by the one person who makes this app.
What happened, or what would you like the app to do?
A short technical record of this device: audio output, measured latency, errors. No recordings, no practice data, nothing that identifies you.
No mail app on this device. The address is copied to the clipboard.
No browser on this device. The link is copied to the clipboard.
No ads, no subscriptions, no accounts, no analytics. The app never talks to a server \u2014 it has no network permission at all.
The microphone listens in real time to hear your hits. Audio is not recorded, not saved and not sent anywhere.
Your progress, settings and practice logs stay on this device. Uninstalling the app deletes them.
A pad plus a metronome in headphones is loud for hours. Keep the volume low enough to hear yourself, and take breaks.
If your hands or wrists hurt, stop. Speed comes from relaxed hands, never from pushing through pain.
